what_new_theme_frame_adds: The new framework converts that fear into specific spending channels: grid investment, backup power, repair, insurance-like redundancy, monitoring, and equipment service.
money_movement_question: Fear of outage moves money into generators, batteries, utility resilience projects, maintenance contracts, backup communications, and financing for hardened infrastructure.
safe_use: Use as a reliability-demand subtheme, not as proof of customer receipts for every resilience vendor.

secondary_new_themes: Capital platforms; Value retail; Healthcare access; Energy affordability and supply route

what_new_theme_frame_adds: The new framework forces the distinction between real customer cash, accounting earnings, debt-funded payouts, and reinvestment needs.
money_movement_question: Customer payments, premiums, fees, fares, spreads, or tolls become operating cash; management then allocates that cash to debt reduction, buybacks, dividends, capex, or acquisitions.
safe_use: Use as a capital-allocation lens across themes, not as proof that payouts are always sustainable.

secondary_new_themes: Capital platforms; Real estate and scarce locations; Healthcare access; Ordinary finance

what_new_theme_frame_adds: The new framework breaks spread economics into route control, legal wrapper, volume, price, funding cost, credit loss, and durability.
money_movement_question: Money moves from end users or counterparties into intermediaries that own the route, balance sheet, network, lease, or contract; the intermediary keeps a fee, spread, tariff, rent, or margin.
safe_use: Use as a cross-sector toll-and-spread subtheme.
next_integration_step: Link it to finance, pipelines, healthcare routing, and scarce-location real estate.

secondary_new_themes: Energy affordability and supply route; Basic materials and input scarcity; Built-environment upkeep

what_new_theme_frame_adds: The new framework asks whether integration actually improves cash conversion or merely adds debt, fixed costs, and operating complexity.
money_movement_question: Capital moves into acquisitions, plants, logistics, fleets, terminals, suppliers, and inventory; cash is supposed to return through better availability, margin, volume, or control.
safe_use: Use as a supply-chain-control subtheme, not as automatic proof of better returns.
next_integration_step: Add to industrial uptime and materials pages with explicit debt and margin checks.

secondary_new_themes: Consumer goods and household identity; Digital control; Ordinary finance
